reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, DeviceUseStatement resource-review context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, the two DeviceUseStatement-scoped behavior findings, representative shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, and the local R4/R6 package definitions. The deterministic aggregate was compared only after forming the resource-level judgment.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `DeviceUseStatement` was trial-use/FMM 0, so there is weak standards-stability pressure to keep the entire legacy resource in R6. That low maturity makes resource retirement more tolerable than it would be for mature or normative clinical content, but it does not make existing device-use histories harmless to lose: status, use timing, reason, body-site, source, and audit/provenance details can still affect clinical interpretation and operational migration.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes `DeviceUseStatement`, so R4 instances need a resource-level migration or archival strategy; compatibility value is mainly in official mapping and status/preservation guidance, not preserving isolated old fields.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual R4-to-R6 shape is resource identity loss rather than a mostly stable resource with local element edits. R4 defines `DeviceUseStatement` as a concrete `DomainResource` for a patient or clinician reported device-use record. In the supplied R6 ballot package there is no `StructureDefinition/DeviceUseStatement`; the exact name appears only as an old type marker, while `DeviceAssociation` is a separate resource for device association or dissociation and not a same-name successor.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: A migration program is unavoidable before ordinary R6 validation or generated-model use. Every R4 payload with `resourceType: "DeviceUseStatement"` must be transformed, retained in an R4 partition, or handled through a non-core compatibility profile. Mapping to `DeviceAssociation` is not a mechanical rename: `identifier`, `device`, and many Patient/Group `subject` cases have plausible homes, but `basedOn`, `derivedFrom`, `timing[x]`, `recordedOn`, `source`, `reasonCode`, `reasonReference`, `bodySite`, `note`, and mandatory status semantics require explicit policy, extensions, linked resources, or preservation of original content.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The root identity break lowers the leverage of preventing additional local breaks. Accepting old status codes or preserving an old child element name would not make a `DeviceUseStatement` instance a native R6 resource. The most compatible base design would have been retaining a deprecated `DeviceUseStatement` resource with its endpoint and search surface, but that is a whole-resource support commitment with duplicate-model and conformance costs. Given FMM 0/trial-use status, `migration-program-dominates` is the right posture, while still requiring careful migration support for safety and audit-relevant information.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The broad less-breaking alternative is a deprecated or compatibility-only R6 `DeviceUseStatement` plus legacy REST/search advertisements. That would preserve old instances but is not low-cost because validators, SDKs, servers, search parameters, route dispatch, and conformance tooling would continue to support a retired model alongside `DeviceAssociation`. More proportionate lower-cost standards work would be official StructureMap/ConceptMap guidance, a status ConceptMap, examples, and standard extension or Provenance guidance for original statement source, recorded time, reasons, timing variants, body site, and notes when the chosen R6 target lacks native slots.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior findings are derivative of resource removal but still operationally real. The base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises a `/DeviceUseStatement` endpoint, and R4 search parameters whose only base was `DeviceUseStatement` disappear with that endpoint. R6 `DeviceAssociation` has analogous `device`, `identifier`, and `subject` search codes, but clients must change resource type, endpoint, result semantics, and sometimes query strategy. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search findings were considered only as ecosystem context because DeviceUseStatement is not the shared base resource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate on the headline: major migration is `Yes`, the shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and the practical compatibility posture is `migration-program-dominates`. My independent review gives explicit weight to the weak R4 FMM/status and to the fact that there are no current Revisit findings, while preserving the important nuance that official mapping, status handling, and endpoint/search transition guidance still matter even though they do not eliminate the resource-identity break.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that the supplied R6 package lacks a native DeviceUseStatement StructureDefinition and that R4 instances therefore cannot validate unchanged. Confidence is lower on production prevalence, official rationale, and the intended successor strategy because the local inputs did not include a ballot rationale, narrative migration note, or authoritative R4-to-R6 ConceptMap.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core package no longer defines DeviceUseStatement
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive finding. R4 instances fail at the root `resourceType` before any child-path issue matters, and generated R6 models, strict validators, server routing, storage partitions, and conformance inventories have no native DeviceUseStatement target. FMM 0 weakens the argument for retaining the resource, but it does not reduce the need for a migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Nearest R6 candidate DeviceAssociation is not a lossless rename of DeviceUseStatement
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This explains why migration is more than changing the resource name. `DeviceAssociation` models association state, while R4 DeviceUseStatement is a reported use statement with provenance-like, timing, reason, body-site, and note fields. That non-isomorphism makes target selection and preservation policy core parts of the resource-level migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Mandatory status codes do not map cleanly to DeviceAssociation.status
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Status conversion is safety- and workflow-relevant because R4's mandatory modifier status includes use-state values such as `completed`, `intended`, `stopped`, and `on-hold`, while R6 DeviceAssociation.status uses a different lifecycle code system. This does not change the resource-level conclusion, but it deserves an official ConceptMap or preservation rule to avoid divergent local mappings.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: DeviceUseStatement is one of the affected removed endpoint resources. The missing advertised endpoint matters for generated clients, conformance tests, route discovery, and compatibility servers, but it is derivative of the resource removal; preserving the endpoint would effectively require a legacy resource or alias policy.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 searches such as `DeviceUseStatement?device=`, `DeviceUseStatement?identifier=`, and `DeviceUseStatement?subject=` no longer have the same R6 base. This is an API migration chore once the target resource is chosen; R6 DeviceAssociation provides similar codes for several of these searches, but endpoint identity and result semantics still change.

findingConsiderations.title: Required input parameter renamed from `input` to `resource`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level operation change may affect cross-version conversion tooling used during DeviceUseStatement migration, but it is not a DeviceUseStatement-specific behavior finding and was not scored as a driver for this resource-level conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish explicit R4 `DeviceUseStatement` migration guidance identifying the intended R6 target or targets, especially when to use `DeviceAssociation` versus Provenance, Observation, retained R4 content, extensions, or other resources.

Provide a computable status ConceptMap and preservation policy for `active`, `completed`, `entered-in-error`, `intended`, `stopped`, and `on-hold`, including guidance for carrying the original R4 status when mapping to `inactive`, `unknown`, `statusReason`, `associationStatus`, or extensions is approximate.

Document field-level mapping examples for `basedOn`, `derivedFrom`, `timing[x]`, `recordedOn`, `source`, reasons, body site, and notes so implementers do not create incompatible local DeviceAssociation profiles or lose clinically relevant context.

Document REST and search transition expectations for retired `/DeviceUseStatement` routes, including whether legacy endpoint/search aliases are implementation-specific compatibility features and how common queries map to DeviceAssociation or another chosen target.

If evidence of substantial production dependence emerges, reconsider a deprecated compatibility resource or legacy endpoint/search alias; absent that evidence, the FMM 0/trial-use baseline makes full resource retention a lower-priority compatibility option.

caveats: The conclusion is based on the supplied R6 6.0.0-ballot4 package; a later package that restores or profiles DeviceUseStatement would change the resource-identity analysis.
The local inputs did not include an official DeviceUseStatement removal rationale, migration guide, or authoritative cross-version ConceptMap.
Production prevalence of R4 DeviceUseStatement use was not established from the supplied local inputs.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context, not as DeviceUseStatement-specific drivers.
